open_obligations: Check whether the strength of easy-to-hard generalization differs across Hase et al.'s datasets and between Sun et al.'s generators and evaluators.
Check difficulty gaps: grade levels versus MATH levels.

out.other_title: Easy-to-hard generalization: LMs often generalize relatively well from easy to hard data
out.rationale: Hase et al. report LMs finetuned or prompted with easy data often do nearly as well on hard data as with hard data. Sun et al. report reward models trained on easy problems (e.g. levels 1-3) can supervise generators on hard problems via re-ranking or RL; Hase et al. study generators directly via ICL, probes and QLoRA, Sun et al. study evaluators, so results should not be transferred between them.

text: The paper's key insight is that an evaluator (reward model) trained on supervision for easier tasks can score candidate solutions to harder tasks, and it proposes training (process-supervised) reward models on easy problems (e.g. MATH levels 1-3) and using them to evaluate policy models on hard problems. It reports that this evaluator generalization enables easy-to-hard generalization in generators through re-ranking or reinforcement learning, with a process-supervised 7b RL model reaching 34.0% and a 34b model with reranking@1024 reaching 52.5% on MATH500 while using human supervision only on easy problems.
title: Easy-to-hard generalization: reward models trained on easy problems supervise hard ones
